question: Should malformed paired-node pullAudio payloads count toward the existing five-consecutive-input-error threshold and terminate the Google Meet bridge?
rationale: Source and proof establish that the implementation works, but only a feature owner can choose between fail-closed contract enforcement and keeping a session alive while repeatedly dropping malformed producer output.

options.title: Keep five-strike shutdown
options.body: Treat malformed chunks as input failures, retaining the submitted bounded fail-closed behavior and existing observability.

options.title: Drop without consuming cutoff
options.body: Reject malformed chunks but keep the bridge alive by separating contract-invalid payloads from transient invocation failures, with focused warning and recovery tests.

options.title: Pause for protocol evidence
options.body: Hold the PR until paired-node version-skew or production evidence clarifies whether malformed output is expected to be recoverable.

recommendation.title: Keep five-strike shutdown
recommendation.body: Treat malformed chunks as input failures, retaining the submitted bounded fail-closed behavior and existing observability.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged feature history ties this person to the Google Meet Chrome/realtime architecture, and the live timeline explicitly routed the availability-risk review there.
